comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## BLOCKER FOUND BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN: the fix cannot land inside the declared file impact

A fix agent traced the record end-to-end before implementing (rather than writing the differ half and
declaring victory) and stopped. Its central finding is CORRECT — I verified it in source myself rather
than accepting the report:

**`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` HARD-DROPS any non-`add` link record.**
At `apply_inbound_records.py:560-562` the loop reads `if entry.get("action") != "add": continue`, and
`rebar.link(...)` is the only call in the function. There is no `rebar.unlink` anywhere on the inbound
path. So a `{"action": "remove", ...}` emitted by `_diff_links_inbound` would be **silently
discarded** — differ-only work would ship the EXACT silent-failure class this epic exists to end: pass
reports OK, dep still present, no traceback. Verified terminus; the outbound `delete_issue_link` path
(`dispatch_one.py`, `batch_dispatch.py`) is a different direction and does not serve this.

Partial mitigation that exists and is NOT sufficient: `apply_handlers.py:274-278` warns when
`links_computed > 0 and links_applied == 0`. That is a TOTAL-no-op detector, so a pass with 1 add +
1 dropped remove stays completely silent, and it is a WARNING, not a failure.

## THE HAZARD THAT MATTERS MORE, and it is not closed by the managed-ref gate

An inbound removal is a WRITE THAT DESTROYS LOCAL DATA. The existing snapshot enrichment is fail-open,
and `fetcher.py:588-590` states its safety argument in so many words:

> "Only entries the search returned a list for are enriched; on any failure the enrichment is skipped
> (differs degrade to 'no Jira links' — **additive ADD-only sync stays safe**) and the pass completes."

**This change VOIDS that argument.** The moment an inbound REMOVE path exists, a failed or truncated
enrichment makes every issue look link-less, and an unguarded removal path would delete every managed
local dep in the project. This epic has already fixed THREE silent-truncation defects in this exact
data path (change 1105; 9263-b404-cb6c-463f; deac-4f5a-856a-49bd, measured losing 92% of a snapshot),
all fail-open and all silent. Turning those READ bugs into a WRITE bug is the worst outcome available
here, and the managed-ref gate does NOT prevent it — that gate protects local-ONLY refs; a MANAGED ref
plus a truncated snapshot is still wrongly deleted.

**The guard, and why it is sound.** Emit a removal only when the issue's link data was POSITIVELY
OBSERVED this pass, detected as `"issuelinks" in jira_fields` (key PRESENT, empty list allowed).
I verified all three legs of this:
 * `fetcher.py:592-596` sets `snapshot[snap_key]["issuelinks"]` ONLY for entries the map returned a
   list for, so key-presence is a reliable "enrichment reached this issue" marker — and the base
   search omits issuelinks entirely (bug 3f04), so nothing else can populate it.
 * Cloud `acli_graph.get_issuelinks_map` does `links = fields.get("issuelinks")` /
   `if isinstance(links, list): result[key] = links`, and Jira returns `issuelinks: []` for a
   link-less issue when the field is requested — so a genuinely link-less issue yields an EMPTY LIST,
   not an absent key.
 * DC `transport.py:391-394` builds `{key: list(... or [])}` for every issue — also key-present.
So key-absent covers exactly the unsafe cases (enrichment failed, the issue fell outside a truncated
page, or the client has no `get_issuelinks_map`) and key-present-empty covers the legitimate
"Jira has zero links" case that must be able to remove.

## `rebar.unlink` HAS NO `relation` PARAMETER — verified, and it is deliberate

`rebar.unlink(id1, id2, *, repo_root=None)` (confirmed by introspection) versus
`rebar.link(id1, id2, relation, ...)`. This is not an oversight: `_commands/unlink.py`'s own usage text
says "pair-scoped, NO relation arg; removes the most-recent link between the pair", and
`_get_link_info` returns "the most recent net-active link for target".

Consequence: if a pair holds TWO active relations and Jira drops only one, a naive
`unlink(local_id, target)` can remove THE WRONG ONE — a link Jira still has. So the apply step must
check that the pair's net-active relation MATCHES the relation whose Jira link vanished, and skip +
log when it does not, rather than removing whatever is most recent. That keeps us from ever deleting a
link the peer still carries, using only the existing pair-scoped API.

## Consequent plan changes (made now)

File impact WIDENED to include `apply_inbound_records.py` — the fix is unshippable without it. Approach
and acceptance criteria added to the description, carrying the three guards above. The plan attestation
is stale after this edit and is being re-reviewed before implementation resumes.

LOC headroom checked: `inbound_differ.py` 718/800 (a ~50-line mirror lands ~770, tight but legal) and
`apply_inbound_records.py` 579/800. `link_direction.py` (59 lines) is the natural seam if the differ
needs to shed weight — both directions already import it.

Two smaller things the implementer must not trip over, both found in the same trace:
 * the same-pass suppression block (`inbound_differ.py:688-703`) filters link mutations by target Jira
   key WITHOUT inspecting `action`, so a new inbound `remove` would be suppressed by an outbound `add`
   to the same key. That is probably the right precedence (local add wins) but it is currently
   ACCIDENTAL, and the comment claims it only drops ADDs. Make it deliberate and say so.
 * `_diff_links_inbound`'s counterpart-absent guard (`local_tickets_by_id.get(target_id) is None →
   continue`) must NOT be reused verbatim on the removal path, or a removal whose counterpart is
   archived is skipped forever.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1276. Guard oracles proven load-bearing by mutation M1.

Four files, 782 insertions: `inbound_differ.py` (`_diff_link_removals_inbound` + G1/G2/G3, G4 made
deliberate), `apply_inbound_records.py` (action branch + `rebar.unlink` + G5), `link_direction.py`
(`observed_peer_deps`), and the new `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py`.
`_managed_refs.py` was NOT changed — the sibling helper was judged to buy naming, not correctness.
`tests/external/` untouched (0-line diff), so `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is unmodified and
should flip GREEN on the next harness run.

### THE LOAD-BEARING MUTATION — M1, all guards removed (unconditional removal)

`6 failed, 11 passed`. **The happy path AND BOTH end-to-end cells still PASS** while every guard cell
fails:

    test_g1_unobserved_issuelinks_emits_no_removal — a removal was inferred from UNOBSERVED link data
    test_g2_unbound_target_emits_no_removal — a dep with an UNBOUND target was removed; the peer never…
    test_g3_unmanaged_dep_emits_no_removal — an UNMANAGED dep was removed — a peer-created or not-yet-pu…
    test_g3_relations_with_no_peer_link_type_are_never_removed[duplicates/supersedes/discovered_from]

That is the whole point, demonstrated rather than argued: **a data-loss implementation passes the
happy-path oracle.** Only the guard oracles catch it. Per-guard mutations M2 (G1 replaced by the
collapsing `.get("issuelinks") or []`) → 1 failed; M3 (G2 deleted) → 1; M4 (G3 deleted) → 4;
M5 (G4 suppression emptied) → 1; M6 (G5 relation-match disabled) → 1, "THE WRONG LINK WAS REMOVED".

### M7 REPRODUCES THE SILENT-FAILURE CLASS ON DEMAND

Restoring the original `action != "add"` drop in the apply layer → `3 failed`, headline
**"THE DEP IS STILL THERE. The peer link was deleted and the record…"** — while the differ still emits
the record. This is the end-to-end proof the blocker analysis demanded: it was also observed naturally
during development, when the differ-only commit went from 6 RED to exactly those 3 RED. G5 predicts the
write using `_get_link_info`, the same function `unlink_core` itself calls, so the prediction cannot
disagree with the write.

All mutations were applied to the FIXED files and restored from the agent's own md5-verified backup
copies — `git checkout --` was never used. Pre-fix RED (committed as `ab8a1a25f2`) was `6 failed,
11 passed`, every message naming the missing removal, no `AttributeError`/`ImportError`.

### MODULE SIZE — inbound_differ.py is at 797/800. THREE LINES OF HEADROOM.

    inbound_differ.py       718 → 797     (first landed at 817, OVER the cap)
    apply_inbound_records.py 579 → 667
    link_direction.py         59 → 89

The 817 overflow was resolved by moving the observed-peer-link set into `link_direction.py` as
`observed_peer_deps`, beside `resolve_inbound_link` and `deps_as_set` — a real seam, not a mechanical
split: rendering the peer set in local relation vocabulary IS the direction problem that module exists
to own. **88d9 modifies the same file and must plan for 3 lines of headroom, not 82** — its plan has
been updated accordingly.

### Regressions and gates

`diffing/` 271 passed; `apply/`+`mutate/`+`conflict/`+`orchestrate/`+7 modules 819 passed; 3 integration
modules 18 passed. `make lint` and `make typecheck` clean.

### GAPS I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN HIDING

 1. **G1's evidence rests on a HAND-MIRRORED COPY of the production enrichment.** The test helper
    `_enrich_like_fetcher` reproduces `fetcher.py:592-596` because that merge is inline in
    `fetch_snapshot` and not extracted, so the real code cannot be called without standing up a
    fetcher. It is byte-faithful today and quotes the original, but **it will silently drift** if that
    loop changes — and G1 is the guard standing between a truncated read and deleted local data. This is
    the weakest link in the change. Filed as a follow-up; extracting the merge is the real fix.
 2. **`rebar.unlink`'s missing `relation` is now a known BEHAVIOURAL limit, not just an API wart.** When
    a pair's net-active relation is not the vanished one, G5 declines and logs rather than removing the
    wrong link. That is the safe direction, but it is a **permanent non-convergence**: the removal
    re-emits and re-declines every pass, with no alert. **I settled the question the implementing agent
    could not**: `graph/_links.add_dependency` is idempotent on `(target_id, relation)` — its own
    docstring says so — while `_get_link_info`/`unlink_core` resolve on TARGET ONLY ("removes the
    most-recent link between the pair"). So two differently-related deps CAN coexist between one pair,
    which makes this gap LIVE rather than theoretical, and G5 is not dead code. Filed as a follow-up.
 3. G3's blind spot is unchanged and is in the commit body: `add_managed_ref` fires on the LINK event, so
    "managed" means created locally, not pushed to the peer. G4 closes it in a healthy pass (outbound
    emits the link ADD and the suppression drops the removal); in a DEGRADED pass — outbound link
    diffing skipped, disabled, or failed while inbound proceeds — a local-only-but-managed dep with a
    bound target can still be removed.
 4. G4 suppresses on `link_remove_keys` as well as `link_add_keys`. The two sets are identical today; the
    choice (never let both directions act on one pair in a pass) is documented but no oracle
    distinguishes them.
 5. Pre-fix, G1-unobserved/G2/G3/G5/steady-state all passed vacuously, because the apply layer dropped
    every removal so nothing could remove anything. Their teeth come entirely from the mutation ledger,
    which is why M1 was run against the FIXED code.

### Process note, recorded because it nearly landed a revert

The agent's `git reset --soft gerrit/main` swept in unrelated landed commits (jira_datacenter adapters,
`_config_schema.py`, two deleted test files), which would have made this change a PARTIAL REVERT of
merged work. It was caught in `git show --stat` before pushing and redone from the original base. The
earlier stack 1272/1273/1274 was ABANDONED in favour of the squashed 1276 because 1272 was RED-only and
could never earn `Verified +1`. A rebase-onto-main push failed twice with a remote-side
`Missing tree 162c59a1` (the tree is present locally), so **1276 is based on `6cdd4b00d9`, not current
main** — correct per the repo's Rebase-If-Necessary rule; Gerrit rebases at submit. The rebased tree was
verified green (271 + 434 tests, lint, typecheck) before that attempt was abandoned.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## THE FIX IS LANDED BUT DOES NOT WORK LIVE — and the cause is an error in MY PLAN, not in the implementation

Harness run **30784592232** against main @ `de2f1ed87` (which CONTAINS this fix, merged as change 1276):
`[jira-live-canary] collected=56 executed=56 skipped=0`, **4 failed / 52 passed** in 23m36s.
`test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is STILL RED:

    AssertionError: the Jira link was DELETED (confirmed absent from the search-backed link read) but
    the local dep on jira-rbjflfv-1 still targets 'jira-rbjflfv-2': deps target ['jira-rbjflfv-2'].
    assert 'jira-rbjflfv-2' not in {'jira-rbjflfv-2'}

(The cell's message text still cites "the inbound link differ is ADD-only" — that string is static prose
written before the fix and is NOT evidence the differ is still add-only. What the assertion PROVES is only
that the removal did not reach the store.)

### ROOT CAUSE: G4 suppresses EVERY legitimate peer-deletion mirror. The rule I specified is wrong.

The landed G4 (`inbound_differ.py:754-781`) drops an inbound `remove` whenever the outbound side has that
target in `link_add_keys`, and its comment states my reasoning verbatim: *"an outbound ADD to this target
means 'being pushed', NOT 'peer deleted it' — never mirror a removal for it."*

**That inference does not hold, and its failure is total rather than partial.** When the peer deletes a
link, the local dep still exists and the peer no longer has it — which is EXACTLY the condition under
which the outbound differ emits a link ADD. So on any bidirectional pass, a peer deletion always produces
an outbound ADD for that target, and G4 therefore always suppresses the inbound REMOVE. **The feature can
never fire.** My plan asserted G4 was needed to close G3's blind spot and called it "not cosmetic"; it is
worse than cosmetic — it is load-bearing in the wrong direction.

The implementation is faithful to the plan and the mutation ledger is sound: `test_g4_outbound_add_this_pass_suppresses_the_removal`
passes because it asserts precisely the behaviour I specified. **A green mutation ledger cannot catch a
wrong specification** — only the live oracle did. That is this epic's own lesson (an oracle can only refute
what it was pointed at) arriving at my expense.

### THE CORRECTED RULE — G3 decides PRECEDENCE; it is not a second AND-gate beside G4

The two directions disagree about the same fact, so one must win, and `managed_refs` is the signal that
says which:
 * ref **IS managed** (we pushed it at some point) and the peer no longer has it → **the peer deleted it**
   → the inbound REMOVE wins, and **the outbound ADD for that pair must be suppressed.**
 * ref is **NOT managed** (never pushed) and the peer does not have it → **we simply have not pushed it**
   → the outbound ADD wins, and the inbound REMOVE is suppressed. (This is the case G4 was written for,
   and it is the only case it should cover.)

Residual risk after the correction: `managed_refs` is monotonic and `seed_managed_refs_from_current` marks
a pre-feature ticket's CURRENT deps as managed, so a never-pushed dep on such a ticket could be read as
"peer deleted it" and removed locally. That window is real and must be recorded — but it is far narrower
than the present behaviour, which is that the feature never works at all.

### SCOPE CONSEQUENCE: the outbound side must change too

Suppressing only the inbound side is not enough. Both differs run against the SAME pre-pass snapshot and
then both apply, so if inbound unlinks locally while outbound still adds the link in Jira, the pass ends
divergent and the next pass re-adopts the link inbound — churn, not convergence. So the managed case must
also stop the outbound ADD. That means `outbound_links.py` (or the shared suppression context) joins the
file impact — this is arbitration across BOTH differs, which the original plan did not contemplate.

### STATUS

Change 1276 is merged and is NOT being reverted: layers 1-3 (the removal differ, the apply-layer action
branch and `rebar.unlink` wiring, G1/G2/G3/G5) are correct and independently mutation-proven, and the
apply-layer drop it fixed was a genuine defect. Only the G3/G4 arbitration is wrong. **This ticket stays
OPEN**; the plan is being amended to the corrected rule, re-reviewed, and a follow-up change will land the
arbitration fix. e369 cannot close until the live cell is green, per this ticket's own acceptance criterion.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== THE AMENDED PLAN IS ALSO WRONG, AND IT WOULD SHIP DATA LOSS. STOP BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. ===

I did not start the implementation. Verifying the plan's one load-bearing premise refuted it, in the
same class as the first failure: an inference about what `managed_refs` MEANS, stated in the plan and
never traced to the code.

--- THE PREMISE, AND WHY IT IS FALSE ---

The amended G4 rule is: "ref IS managed + peer lacks it -> the peer DELETED it -> inbound REMOVE wins
and the outbound ADD is suppressed." The plan justifies its safety with: "an UNMANAGED dep is never
removed (the outbound ADD wins), so a brand-new local dep is safe by construction."

**A brand-new local dep is NOT unmanaged.** The plan says so itself, two paragraphs earlier, and the
two statements contradict each other: `add_managed_ref` is folded by the LINK-event processor
(`reducer/_processors.py:411`, inside `process_link`), so a ref is managed THE INSTANT IT IS CREATED
LOCALLY. `should_propagate_removal` (`_managed_refs.py:140-153`) is nothing but
`(kind, target) in managed_ref_set(local_ticket)` — no push, no peer, no history.

So the residual window the plan describes as narrow ("chiefly `seed_managed_refs_from_current`, a
PRE-FEATURE ticket's current deps") is not narrow at all. It is EVERY locally created link, from the
moment of creation until it is pushed.

--- MEASURED, NOT REASONED (probe run against gerrit/main @ b6916709f3) ---

Drove the reducer and the production differ directly:

  after a LOCAL link event, managed_refs = [['blocks', 'local-b']]
  should_propagate_removal('blocks','local-b') = True

  (a) _diff_link_removals_inbound, brand-new never-pushed dep, issuelinks observed []
        -> [{'action': 'remove', 'target_id': 'local-b', 'relation': 'blocks'}]
  (b) compute_inbound_mutations, no outbound context
        -> [{'action': 'remove', 'target_id': 'local-b', 'relation': 'blocks'}]
  (c) compute_inbound_mutations, WITH the outbound link ADD a real bidirectional pass emits
        -> []

Read (c) against (b): **the landed G4 outbound-add suppression is the ONLY thing standing between a
brand-new local link and its deletion.** The amended plan's central instruction is to delete that
suppression. Doing so turns a dormant feature into an active data-loss bug on the ORDINARY CREATE
PATH: a human creates a link locally, the first reconcile pass emits an inbound REMOVE (managed +
peer lacks it), the arbitration suppresses the outbound ADD, and the link is destroyed instead of
pushed. That is strictly worse than today's no-op.

--- WHY NO PATCH TO THE RULE CAN FIX THIS (the part that decides the ticket) ---

The two scenarios are STATE-IDENTICAL:
  * a brand-new local link never pushed to the peer, and
  * a link rebar pushed that the peer then deleted
both present exactly `managed = True`, `target bound = True`, `issuelinks observed = True`, `peer link
absent = True`. Every input the guards read is the same in both. Therefore ANY arbitration that is a
function of (managed, bound, observed, current peer set) MUST return the same answer for both, and one
of those answers is data loss. This is not a tuning problem; it is a missing-signal problem.

The discriminator can only be HISTORY: "was this link ever on the peer" or "did we ever push it".
Neither is persisted today. `should_propagate_removal` cannot supply it; that is the whole finding.

Note what this means for the existing green test `test_peer_deleted_link_emits_a_removal`: its input
is the brand-new-link state. It is named for one scenario and pins both. That is the same failure the
first version had — the oracle asserts the specification, and the specification cannot see the
difference.

--- WHAT THE LANDED CODE (1276) ACTUALLY DOES TODAY, stated plainly ---

The feature is dormant and the pass is SAFE. A link deleted in Jira is re-created by the outbound ADD
on the next pass: local-wins, convergent, no local data loss, and the human's Jira-side deletion is
silently reverted. That is a real divergence from the AC, and it FAILS SAFE.

--- THE ONE CORRECT DESIGN I CAN SEE, AND ITS COST ---

Arbitrate on the PREVIOUS PEER LINK SET: link present in the prior pass's peer snapshot AND absent now
= a real remote deletion; absent in both = never pushed, so the outbound ADD wins. Brand-new deps are
then safe BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a gate, and `managed_refs` drops out of the arbitration
entirely (it can stay as a belt-and-braces gate).

The plan rejected this as "a new persisted artifact with its own migration and truncation semantics".
That cost is lower than stated, and the ticket should be re-planned knowing it:
  * the artifact ALREADY EXISTS and is already written and committed every pass —
    `_write_prev_snapshot_key_set` (`reconcile.py:538-541`) writes `{jira_key: {}}` to
    `.bridge_state/prev.json`. This is one added field per key, not a new file.
  * migration is trivially fail-safe: an old `prev.json` has no link data, so nothing is provable, so
    NO removal fires; it self-heals after one pass.
  * truncation is fail-safe on both legs: current-pass enrichment missing -> G1 already declines;
    prior-pass enrichment missing -> presence unprovable -> decline.
  * the narrowing was deliberate (2cc0-da4a-d736-4ba2, "Narrow persisted Jira snapshot to key
    membership ... while RETAINING FULL PER-PASS SNAPSHOTS") and was about DETERMINISM of the
    persisted prev state. Widening it re-opens that question and must answer it, not ignore it — but
    note the full per-pass snapshots are retained on disk, so the raw signal is already being captured.

--- STATUS ---

Implementation NOT started, deliberately. The certified plan cannot be implemented as written without
shipping the defect above, and `review-plan` certified it because the plan is internally consistent
about a false premise — the gate reads the plan, not the reducer.

Awaiting the operator's call on build-the-history-signal vs. leave-the-feature-dormant-and-document.
Whichever is chosen, the plan needs a fresh amendment and a fresh review round; and per this ticket's
own AC, the live cell is the arbiter, so nothing here is settled by a green unit suite.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== ADDENDUM: THE HISTORY SIGNAL ALREADY EXISTS, IS ALREADY PERSISTED, AND IS ALREADY GOVERNED BY AN ADR ===

Correcting my own cost estimate in the previous comment (I proposed widening `.bridge_state/prev.json`).
There is a better home, and it makes the "build it correctly" option materially cheaper than either that
proposal or the plan's rejected alternative. Traced in the code, not inferred:

**ADR 0026's per-binding BASELINE — "the last-synced Jira-side values" — stored on the binding entry.**
  * `binding_store.set_baseline(local_id, fields)` (`binding_store.py:453-467`) records it; the entry key
    is `baseline`; it is **in-memory until `save()`, persisted by the EXISTING binding-store commit path,
    "no new commit surface (ADR 0026 §Consequences)"**.
  * `reconcile._advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:519-536`) runs **EVERY PASS**, advancing every
    `confirmed` binding whose key is in the current fetch window to the current snapshot. So the
    artifact is not just present — it is already maintained on exactly the cadence this arbitration
    needs.
  * **The absence semantics are ALREADY the fail-safe we need, and already documented:** "An ABSENT
    baseline is VALID and degrades to local-wins (safe/lossy); a version-1 store (no baselines) reads
    fine" (`binding_store.py:101-105`). No baseline -> no proof the peer ever had the link -> no removal.
    That is the migration story, already written, already shipped.

So the arbitration becomes a HISTORY comparison with no new artifact and no new commit surface:
  * link in the binding's last-synced peer link set, and ABSENT from the current OBSERVED set
      -> the peer DELETED it -> inbound REMOVE wins, and the outbound ADD for that pair is suppressed.
  * link NOT in the baseline -> we have never seen it on the peer -> **it is a local link we have not
      pushed** -> outbound ADD wins, no removal. Brand-new deps are safe BY CONSTRUCTION, which is what
      the amended plan claimed and could not deliver.
  * baseline absent (v1 store, unconfirmed binding, out-of-window key) -> local-wins -> no removal.
  * current enrichment unobserved -> G1 already declines, unchanged.

`managed_refs` then drops OUT of the arbitration entirely — which is the right outcome, because it
cannot answer the question being asked. Keep G3 if desired as a belt-and-braces gate; do not let it
decide.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES for whoever writes the amendment:
  * store the peer link set under its OWN key on the binding entry with its own accessor — do NOT add
    `issuelinks` to `_BASELINE_FIELDS` (`binding_store.py:106-112`), which is the 5-scalar three-way-merge
    vocabulary consumed by `outbound_field_diff` and `binding_walk`; widening it would perturb that merge.
  * store it in LOCAL RELATION vocabulary (`[[relation, local_target_id], ...]`) via the same
    `link_direction` translation both differs already use, so the comparison never touches raw peer keys
    (the direction/vocabulary trap the plan already documents).
  * only advance the recorded set when the current pass OBSERVED issuelinks for that key (G1 semantics),
    or a failed enrichment would overwrite a good history with an empty one and manufacture the very
    "peer deleted everything" reading G1 exists to prevent. **This is the load-bearing detail of the
    whole design — a fail-open READ must not be allowed to poison the history.**
  * plumbing: `prev_snapshot` reaches `outbound_field_diff` today but NOT the link differs, whereas
    `binding_store` is ALREADY passed to both `_diff_links`/`_diff_link_removals` and
    `_diff_link_removals_inbound`. That asymmetry is a second reason to prefer the baseline over the
    snapshot: **the arbitration needs no new parameter on either differ.**

COST, honestly: one new binding-entry field + accessor, one advance site next to `_advance_baselines`
(gated on observation), the arbitration in both differs, plus the ledger and a harness run. Bigger than
a one-line guard flip; much smaller than the "new persisted artifact with its own migration and
truncation semantics" the plan declined on.

This does not decide the ticket — deferring the feature and documenting local-wins is still a legitimate
call, since today's landed behaviour fails safe. It only corrects the price of building it right.

comments.body:
=== SCOPING FACT, VERIFIED: THIS IS A SHARED-CORE GAP, IDENTICAL ON CLOUD. IT IS NOT A DC DEFECT. ===

Traced rather than assumed, because it decides whether this ticket gates e369 at all:

 * `compute_inbound_mutations` has exactly ONE call site — `run_differs.py:641` — in the backend-agnostic
   core. Nothing about it is DC-specific.
 * both backends implement the same port method the link diff consumes: `map_remote_links` on
   `JiraBackend` (`adapters/jira/backend.py:219`) and on `JiraDataCenterBackend`
   (`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:397`), against `_backend.py:469`.
 * therefore a link deleted on the peer is NOT mirrored locally on **Cloud** either, and has never been.
   The behaviour is local-wins-and-resurrect on both backends, identically.

**Why only DC noticed.** The DC suite has the cell; the Cloud suite does not. Cloud's live link coverage is
three cells — `test_link_primitives_roundtrip_live`, `test_link_sync_differ_apply_roundtrip_live`,
`test_link_sync_writes_absolute_direction_live` — and NONE of them deletes a link on the peer and asserts
the local dep goes away. The only `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` in the repo is DC's
(`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py:874`).

So this defect was not introduced by DC support and is not a DC/Cloud divergence. It surfaced because J11's
mutation table is MORE comprehensive than the Cloud suite it was built to reach parity with — the parity
work finding a pre-existing shared-core gap is the parity work succeeding, not DC shipping broken.

CONSEQUENCE FOR e369's SCOPE: on the operator's stated priority — defect-free **DC** functionality, and DC
testing at parity with existing Jira testing — this ticket is not a DC-confidence blocker. DC is not worse
than Cloud here; both share one semantic that fails safe (a peer-side deletion is reverted on the next
pass; no local data is destroyed). That is the same shape as the `e39f` ruling.

AND A PARITY FOLLOW-UP FALLS OUT OF IT: the Cloud suite is missing the inbound-link-deletion cell that DC
has. Whichever way this ticket is decided, Cloud should get the equivalent cell so the two suites agree
about what is and is not covered — otherwise the next reader concludes from a green Cloud suite that Cloud
mirrors peer deletions, which it does not. That belongs to the parity epic 3e73-72b5-cff2-40f0.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== OSS / ECOSYSTEM RESEARCH, BY OPERATOR DIRECTION: IS MIRRORING A PEER-SIDE LINK DELETION A PARITY GAP? ===

The operator's decision rule: "How do popular and actively maintained OSS projects with Jira integration
handle this? If this is a parity gap, build it now. If we would be implementing something that's not
commonly handled, defer it."

**FINDING: it is NOT commonly handled. Baseline behaviour across the field is additive / one-way for
RELATIONSHIP deletions, and the tools that deliberately refuse it cite exactly the risk we just lived
through.**

Evidence gathered:

 * **Aha!** states the design decision outright: it does not delete records based on updates from
   integrations, "because there is too much risk of users inadvertently deleting data, especially when
   they are just getting started."
   https://big.ideas.aha.io/ideas/A-I-8761
 * **Asana <-> Jira** (first-party, actively maintained bidirectional sync): when an item is deleted in
   one tool it STILL EXISTS in the other, merely without the connection. Deletion does not propagate.
   https://forum.asana.com/t/jira-integration-deleting-task-still-exists/1030319
 * **Adobe Workfront <-> Jira**: deleting on the Workfront side does not delete or deactivate the linked
   Jira item; users report it and it is answered as expected behaviour, not a bug.
   https://experienceleaguecommunities.adobe.com/adobe-workfront-23/jira-integrations-when-deleting-something-from-workfront-it-doesn-t-push-to-jira-is-the-config-not-set-up-correctly-or-is-this-a-know-bug-still-shows-as-active-task-issue-in-jira-120914
 * **Atlassian's OWN first-party tooling is unreliable here**: there is a support KB for "the Delete
   Issue Links action does not delete any link" in Automation for Jira — i.e. even Atlassian's native
   link-deletion primitive has a documented failure mode.
   https://support.atlassian.com/automation/kb/delete-issue-links-action-does-not-delete-any-link/
 * **Exalate** — the most capable tool in this space, and the one that CAN mirror links — treats issue-link
   sync as an ADVANCED, OPT-IN, SCRIPTED behaviour, not a default: link sync must be explicitly
   configured, every linked issue must be synchronised separately to preserve the association, and
   support advises manually DISCONNECTING a pair BEFORE archiving rather than relying on propagation.
   https://docs.exalate.com/docs/how-to-synchronize-issue-links-on-jira-on-premise
   https://docs.exalate.com/docs/jira-cloud-issue-link-sync
   https://community.exalate.com/t/delete-remote-link-when-archiving-an-issue/6775

**READ AGAINST OUR OWN SITUATION.** Two things follow, and they point the same way:

 1. This is NOT a Cloud/DC parity gap either. Verified earlier on this ticket: `compute_inbound_mutations`
    has ONE call site in backend-agnostic core and both backends implement the same `map_remote_links`
    port, so Cloud does not mirror peer link deletions and never has. DC is not behind Cloud, and rebar
    is not behind the field — the field mostly declines to do this on purpose.
 2. **We now have first-hand evidence for why.** The sibling defect on 88d9 shipped the same inference
    (peer absence + our own provenance marker = a deletion) and destroyed 63 parent edges on its first
    production pass. Aha!'s stated rationale is not hypothetical caution; it is precisely our incident.

**CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TICKET: DEFER THE BUILD**, per the operator's rule. Concretely that means rebar's
shipped semantics for a peer-side link deletion are LOCAL-WINS-AND-RESTORE — the link is re-added on the
next pass — which is convergent, loses no local data, is identical on both backends, and is in line with
mature tools in this space rather than behind them.

What the deferral does NOT mean: it does not mean the analysis is discarded. The correct design is known
and now has a working template — the per-binding peer-state record that change 1296 introduced for
parents (`get_peer_parent`/`set_peer_parent`, advanced only on OBSERVATION). A link version is the same
shape and `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs, so whoever picks this up starts
from a proven pattern rather than from the refuted `managed_refs` premise.

Recorded so the next reader does not re-litigate it from scratch, and so a green Cloud suite is not
mistaken for coverage that does not exist (Cloud has NO inbound-link-deletion cell at all — filed
separately for the parity epic).

comments.body:
## AC AMENDMENT — the removal-mirroring criteria are RETIRED, and what replaces them

Operator ruling applied: research the ecosystem, build if it is a parity gap, defer if it is not
commonly handled. The research (previous comment) found it is NOT commonly handled. So the ACs written
around "the removal IS emitted" no longer describe what this ticket ships, and pretending otherwise
would leave a permanently-red live cell and a ticket whose criteria can never be ticked.

**RETIRED** (they specify a feature deliberately not shipped — recorded, not silently dropped):
 * a link deleted in Jira is mirrored locally / the local dep is positively absent after the pass
 * the removal record survives the apply layer end to end
 * G1 observed-empty EMITS the removal; G2/G3/G4/G5 gating of that removal
 * the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is GREEN on a harness run
 * "the mutation set MUST include making the removal unconditional"

**WHAT THIS TICKET ACTUALLY SHIPPED, and what now stands as its criteria:**
 - [x] the apply-layer DROP is fixed. `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` used to
       discard any non-`add` link record outright (`action != "add": continue`), so even a correct
       differ could not have worked. That branch + the `rebar.unlink` wiring landed in 1276 and is
       independently mutation-proven. This was a REAL defect and it is fixed.
 - [x] G1/G2/G3/G5 landed and are mutation-proven. They are dormant (nothing emits a removal for them
       to gate) but they are correct, and they are the guards a future implementation needs.
 - [x] the shipped semantics are STATED: local-wins-and-restore. A link deleted in Jira is re-added on
       the next pass — convergent, no local data destroyed, identical on both backends.
 - [x] the live cell is XFAIL with the full reason in the marker (change 1303), NOT inverted and NOT
       deleted, so it fails loudly as an xpass the moment a removal path starts working.
 - [x] the ecosystem evidence is recorded, with sources, so this is not re-litigated from scratch.
 - [x] **the refutation of the original design is recorded, with a probe** — `managed_refs` cannot
       distinguish "a link we never pushed" from "a link the peer deleted"; the two states are
       IDENTICAL on every input the guards read. That is the finding that stopped a second data-loss
       defect before it was written.
 - [x] **the correct design is recorded WITH A WORKING TEMPLATE.** Change 1296 landed exactly this
       pattern for parents — a per-binding record of what the peer last had, advanced only on
       OBSERVATION — so whoever picks this up starts from shipped, reviewed code rather than from the
       refuted premise. `binding_store` is already a parameter of both link differs, so no new differ
       parameter is needed.

**WHY THIS IS NOT "AMENDING AWAY AN INCONVENIENT AC".** The distinction the operator drew on 5200's
row 12 was: do not amend away a COVERAGE gap. This is not that. The cell exists and still runs; what
changed is the product decision about what behaviour to ship, taken on ecosystem evidence plus a
first-hand incident in which the identical inference destroyed 63 parent edges. The behaviour is
documented rather than quietly absent, and the loud-on-xpass marker means a future fix cannot land
unnoticed.

**RESIDUAL RISK, stated plainly:** a link deleted in Jira comes back. A user who deletes a link in Jira
and does not also unlink locally will see it reappear. That is a real divergence from user intent, it is
NOT DC-specific, and it is the behaviour every comparable tool in this space also ships.

Closes when 1303 lands.

compiled_state.description:
# An issue link DELETED in Jira is never removed from the local ticket (inbound)

Found while writing the row-11 inbound cell of the J11 mutation table
(story 5200-e04e-246e-4aae), filed per that story's rule that a cell revealing a
product defect stops and reports. THIS TICKET NOW CARRIES THE FIX (reparented under
epic e369-a449-4773-48fb by operator ruling).

## Mechanism

The inbound link differ is ADD-ONLY, by construction and by its own docstring.
`inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound` opens with "Reflect Jira issuelinks into rebar
relations. ADD-only." and closes with "ADD-only (no REMOVE mutations)"
(src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py:380 and :396). It iterates
the CURRENT `fields.issuelinks` and emits an add per unseen link; nothing walks the
local deps looking for one whose Jira counterpart has gone.

So the flow is asymmetric: the OUTBOUND direction does have a removal path
(`outbound_links._diff_link_removals`, which emits
`{"action": "remove", "type":..., "to_key":..., "relation":...}`,
outbound_links.py:120-175, applied via `delete_issue_link`), while the inbound
direction has no counterpart. A link a human deletes in Jira stays on the rebar
ticket forever, and no pass ever reports it.

## Why this is a gap and not merely a documented design choice

Story 5200's acceptance criteria define a 14-row mutation table with an explicit
oracle per direction. Row 11's INBOUND oracle is "that link is ABSENT" from the
local ticket. That row cannot pass while the differ is add-only, so the epic's
comprehensiveness claim is not reachable without either implementing the removal
or amending the AC. This ticket IMPLEMENTS THE REMOVAL; the Approach below resolves
the evidence question (how we know the peer deleted a link rather than that we failed
to observe it), which is the part that made this more than a guard removal.

Note the add-only choice is not obviously safe either: the same docstring's
idempotency logic already skips an emit when "the counterpart is absent from the
ACTIVE local set", i.e. the differ is willing to reason about absence — just not
about the absence of the LINK.

## Expected failure

`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips`
asserts the local dep is gone after the Jira link is deleted. It should go RED on
the harness until this is addressed.

## Approach

Mirror the outbound removal path, but gate it — an inbound removal is a WRITE that destroys local
data, so the whole design problem is establishing that the peer really DELETED the link rather than
that we merely failed to see it.

1. **A new `_diff_link_removals_inbound` in `inbound_differ.py`**, the mirror of
   `outbound_links._diff_link_removals` (outbound_links.py:120-175). It walks the local `deps` and
   emits `{"action": "remove", "target_id": <local id>, "relation": <local relation>}` — inbound
   records carry `target_id` (a local id), not `to_key`. Build the OBSERVED peer link set through
   `link_direction.resolve_inbound_link`, NOT from raw Jira keys, so both sides are compared in local
   relation vocabulary; comparing raw keys makes an `inwardIssue`/`Blocks` link read as `depends_on`
   while the local dep is `blocks`, producing a spurious removal of a link that is still there.

2. **`apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links` must branch on `action`.** It currently reads
   `if entry.get("action") != "add": continue` (apply_inbound_records.py:560-562) and only ever calls
   `rebar.link`, so a removal record is silently discarded — a differ-only fix would ship the exact
   silent-failure class this epic exists to end. Removal applies via `rebar.unlink`.

### The five guards, and why each is load-bearing

- **G1 OBSERVED.** Emit only when `"issuelinks" in jira_fields` — key PRESENT, empty list allowed.
  `fetcher.py:592-596` sets that key only for entries `get_issuelinks_map` returned a list for, and the
  base search omits issuelinks entirely (bug 3f04), so key-presence is a reliable "enrichment reached
  this issue" marker. Both readers make an empty list authoritative rather than dropping the key
  (Cloud `acli_graph.get_issuelinks_map` records `result[key] = links` for any list "including the
  empty list — an authoritative 'no links'"; DC `transport.py:391-394` builds `{key: list(... or [])}`).
  `_snapshot_schema.py` is `total=False` and never injects `[]`. So key-absent covers exactly the
  unsafe cases — enrichment failed, HTTP 410, a fail-open partial map, the issue fell outside a
  truncated page, a cross-project bound issue, or a client with no `get_issuelinks_map` — and every one
  of those fails safe to NO REMOVAL.
  **`_diff_links_inbound:397` opens `jira_fields.get("issuelinks") or []`, which collapses
  observed-empty into unobserved. That line must NOT be reused on the removal path.**
- **G2 TARGET BOUND.** Require `binding_store.get_jira_key(target_id)` non-None. An unbound target
  could never have had a Jira link, so its absence proves nothing.
- **G3 MANAGED.** `should_propagate_removal(relation, target_id, local_ticket)` from
  `rebar.reducer._managed_refs` — the same predicate the outbound parent/link gates consume, so a
  peer-created dep rebar never owned is not clobbered. It also excludes
  `duplicates`/`supersedes`/`discovered_from` for free, because `MANAGED_REF_KINDS` omits relations
  with no reliable peer link type; do NOT add a redundant filter for them.
- **G4 ARBITRATION — REWRITTEN AFTER THE LIVE ORACLE REFUTED THE FIRST VERSION. READ THIS CAREFULLY.**
  The FIRST version of this guard said: "never mirror a removal for a target the outbound side is adding
  this pass", on the reasoning that an outbound ADD means "being pushed" rather than "peer deleted it".
  **That reasoning is WRONG, and its failure is total.** When the peer deletes a link, the local dep still
  exists and the peer lacks it — which is EXACTLY the condition under which the outbound differ emits a
  link ADD. So on any bidirectional pass a peer deletion always produces an outbound ADD for that target,
  and the guard therefore always suppressed the inbound REMOVE: **the feature could never fire.** Proven by
  harness run 30784592232 against main @ `de2f1ed87` (which CONTAINS change 1276):
  `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` stayed RED with "the Jira link was DELETED … but the local dep …
  still targets 'jira-rbjflfv-2'". The mutation ledger was green throughout, because
  `test_g4_outbound_add_this_pass_suppresses_the_removal` asserted the behaviour the plan specified — **a
  mutation ledger cannot catch a wrong SPECIFICATION.**

  **THE CORRECTED RULE: `managed_refs` decides PRECEDENCE between the two directions. It is not a second
  AND-gate beside G3.** The two differs disagree about one fact — local dep present, peer link absent — and
  exactly one must win:
    * ref **IS managed** (rebar pushed it at some point) + peer lacks it → **the peer DELETED it** → the
      inbound REMOVE wins, **and the outbound ADD for that pair must be suppressed.**
    * ref is **NOT managed** (never pushed) + peer lacks it → **we simply have not pushed it yet** → the
      outbound ADD wins and the inbound REMOVE is suppressed. This is the ONLY case the old G4 should have
      covered.
  Suppressing only the inbound side is NOT sufficient and must not be shipped: both differs run against
  the same pre-pass snapshot and then both apply, so inbound unlinking locally while outbound re-adds in
  Jira leaves the pass DIVERGENT and the next pass re-adopts the link inbound — churn, not convergence.
  **So `outbound_links.py` (or the shared suppression context) is in scope: this is arbitration across BOTH
  differs.**
  An outbound REMOVE for the same pair still suppresses the inbound removal (the two directions must not
  both act on one pair in a pass; deferring re-evaluates next pass rather than double-removing).
- **G5 RELATION MATCH AT APPLY.** `rebar.unlink(id1, id2, *, repo_root=None)` takes NO relation
  argument, and that is deliberate — `_commands/unlink.py`'s usage text says "pair-scoped, NO relation
  arg; removes the most-recent link between the pair", and `_get_link_info` returns the most recent
  net-active link. So if a pair holds two active relations and the peer dropped only one, a naive
  unlink can remove THE WRONG ONE — a link the peer still has. The apply step must confirm the pair's
  net-active relation MATCHES the vanished relation, and skip + log otherwise.

### G3's blind spot, stated plainly rather than papered over

`add_managed_ref` is folded by the **LINK-event** processor (`reducer/_processors.py:411`), so a ref
becomes "managed" the instant it is created LOCALLY — it does NOT mean "we pushed it to the peer".
`seed_managed_refs_from_current` compounds this for pre-feature tickets by seeding all current `deps`
as managed. So G3 alone does not establish that the peer ever had the link. **Under the CORRECTED arbitration rule above, that is handled by precedence rather than by a second gate:** an UNMANAGED dep is never removed (the outbound ADD wins), so a brand-new local dep is safe by construction. What remains is the narrower case where `managed_refs` says managed but the ref was never actually pushed — chiefly `seed_managed_refs_from_current`, which marks a PRE-FEATURE ticket's CURRENT deps as managed. On such a ticket a never-pushed dep could be read as "the peer deleted it" and removed locally. That window is real and is recorded here deliberately; it is far narrower than the behaviour it replaces, which was that the feature never fired at all.

**The earlier text here claimed "G4 closes that in a healthy pass, because outbound emits a link ADD for exactly that dep and the suppression drops the removal." That sentence was the error** — it is precisely why the first implementation could never work, and it is retained in this form only so the mistake is legible rather than quietly overwritten.

**Alternative rejected: compare against the previous peer link set** (link present in the prior Jira
snapshot, absent now = a real remote deletion). This is the textbook-correct signal and would retire
G3's blind spot outright, but it is NOT available: as of `6cdd4b00d9` ("Narrow persisted Jira snapshot
to key membership") `reconcile._write_prev_snapshot_key_set` persists `{jira_key: {}}` — key membership
only, carrying no fields and therefore no issuelinks. Reaching for it means adding a new persisted
artifact with its own migration and its own truncation semantics, which is a materially larger change
than this defect warrants. Recorded so a future reader knows it was considered and why it was declined.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_differ.py` — the removal differ + G1/G2/G3, and making
  G4 deliberate. 718/800 LOC today; a ~50-line mirror lands ~770. If it would breach 800, shed weight
  into `link_direction.py` (59 LOC, already imported by both directions), never mechanically.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_records.py` — action branch + `rebar.unlink` + G5.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_links.py` (or the shared same-pass suppression context) —
  **ADDED after the live refutation:** the managed case must also suppress the OUTBOUND link ADD, or the
  pass ends divergent and churns. This is the arbitration half the original plan did not contemplate.
  579/800 LOC.
- `src/rebar/reducer/_managed_refs.py` — OPTIONAL, only to add a `should_mirror_peer_removal` sibling
  sharing the `managed_ref_set()` read path. Mechanically the identical predicate, so it buys naming
  and a place to document that inbound needs more than the managed check. Skip it if the guards read
  clearly without it.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py` (new).
- **Out of scope:** any fetcher or adapter change (the observed/unobserved distinction already
  survives); `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py`, which another ticket owns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] a link deleted in Jira is mirrored locally: the local dep is asserted POSITIVELY ABSENT after
      the pass, never "no exception was raised"
- [ ] the removal record survives the apply layer end to end — differ emit → `run_differs` payload →
      `apply_inbound` → `rebar.unlink` → the dep is gone from the reduced ticket. A test that stops at
      the differ boundary does NOT satisfy this, because the record was silently dropped at
      `apply_inbound_records.py:560-562` and a differ-only oracle goes green while the store is untouched
- [ ] G1: with the issue's `issuelinks` key ABSENT (unobserved — simulate the real truncation/fail-open
      shape, not a hand-deleted key if the real path differs), NO removal is emitted
- [ ] G1: with `issuelinks` present and EMPTY (authoritative "no links"), the removal IS emitted
- [ ] G2: an unbound target emits no removal
- [ ] G3: a dep that is not in `managed_refs` emits no removal, so a peer-created dep is never clobbered
- [ ] G4 arbitration, MANAGED case: a MANAGED dep whose peer link is gone emits the removal **even
      though the outbound side is adding that target this pass**, and the outbound ADD for that pair is
      SUPPRESSED. Assert BOTH halves — inbound removal present AND outbound add absent — because
      suppressing only one leaves the pass divergent and churning
- [ ] G4 arbitration, UNMANAGED case: an UNMANAGED dep whose peer link is absent emits NO removal and the
      outbound ADD proceeds, asserted against `link_add_keys`
- [ ] a test pins that the two arbitration branches are decided by `managed_refs` and NOT by the mere
      presence of an outbound add — i.e. flipping only the managed-ness of the ref flips which direction
      wins. This is the assertion whose absence let the first version ship broken
- [ ] the live cell `test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is GREEN on a harness run, and the run id is
      recorded here. **A green unit suite is explicitly NOT sufficient for this ticket** — the first
      version had a fully green, mutation-checked unit suite and did not work at all
- [ ] G5: when the pair's net-active relation differs from the vanished relation, no unlink is
      performed and the skip is logged
- [ ] steady state does not churn: a managed dep still present on the peer emits NO removal on
      repeated passes
- [ ] every oracle is MUTATION-CHECKED with verdicts recorded on this ticket, and the mutation set
      MUST include making the removal unconditional — a fix that emits removals with no guard passes
      the happy-path oracle while being a data-loss bug, so the guard oracles are the ones that
      actually protect the product
- [ ] `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py::test_inbound_delete_link_round_trips` is
      unmodified, and turns GREEN on the harness once this lands
- [ ] `inbound_differ.py` and `apply_inbound_records.py` each stay under the 800-LOC cap

the managed case must also suppress the OUTBOUND link ADD, or inbound unlinks locally while outbound re-adds in Jira and the pass churns
already landed in 1276 (action branch + rebar.unlink + G5); listed because the arbitration fix may need to touch the apply path
the G4 cell must be rewritten: it currently asserts the WRONG behaviour, and its greenness is why the first version shipped broken

compiled_state.title: Inbound link removal is never mirrored (inbound link differ is ADD-only)
